verdict.rationale: Isaac's core purpose is a simulated test environment kept separate from real robots: Isaac Sim lets developers evaluate end-to-end systems through software-in-the-loop or hardware-in-the-loop testing, validate robot stacks with ROS 2, and plug into existing testing and validation pipelines. It also supports repeatable Docker setups and headless, scriptable runs that agents or automation can drive. Missing for 10: no explicit documentation of isolation from production or real-world data (the sandbox-versus-production framing is only implied by simulation), no independent hands-on corroboration of the testing workflow, and no agent-specific guidance for running isolated test sessions.
